policy_title: Clinical Policy CP.MP.107: Durable Medical Equipment and Orthotics and Prosthetics Guidelines (Rev. 08/26)
source_quote: Medically necessary for arch, heel, or other foot pain when meeting both of the following: A. Foot condition, as indicated by one of the following: 1. Juvenile idiopathic arthritis; 2. Pes cavus (high arch); 3. Rheumatoid arthritis; 4. Plantar fasciitis when symptoms have been present for at least one month; 5. Posterior tibial tendon dysfunction in adult, as indicated by one or more of the following: a. Stage I disease (tenosynovitis without deformity); b. Stage II disease (flexible and passively correctable deformity); B. Documentation that adjustment of activities, anti-inflammatory medications, prefabricated orthotics, stretching of calf muscles and plantar surface have failed to improve symptoms.

criteria.description: Qualifying foot condition (JIA, pes cavus, RA, plantar fasciitis ≥1 month, or PTTD Stage I/II)
Failure of conservative care: activity adjustment, NSAIDs, prefab orthotics, and stretching

required_documentation: Clinical notes documenting foot condition and duration
Documentation detailing failure of activity adjustment, medications, prefab inserts, and stretching
review_notes: Plantar fasciitis requires ≥1 month duration. PTTD limited to Stage I or II.

policy_title: Clinical Policy CP.MP.107: Durable Medical Equipment and Orthotics and Prosthetics Guidelines (Rev. 08/26)
source_quote: Medically necessary when ordered immediately post-operative for orthopedic surgeries such as rotator cuff repair, tendon repair, or ORIF. Replacement with the same or similar item due to normal wear and tear is considered medically necessary when the orthotic is still needed.
clinical_service_or_procedure: Shoulder, elbow, wrist, hand, finger orthotics (HCPCS L3904, L4000, L4010, L4020, L4030, L4205)

criteria.description: Ordered immediately post-operative for orthopedic surgery (rotator cuff, tendon repair, ORIF)
Replacement due to normal wear and tear when orthotic is still medically needed

required_documentation: Operative report or surgical discharge plan
Replacement order documenting ongoing medical need
review_notes: Covers immediate post-op period and normal wear/tear replacements.

policy_title: Clinical Policy CP.MP.107: Durable Medical Equipment and Orthotics and Prosthetics Guidelines (Rev. 08/26)
source_quote: Medically necessary when the request specific criteria in A. or B. are met: A. Initial request meets all of the following: 1. Functional needs cannot be met with activity modification and compensatory techniques; 2. Requested prosthesis is anticipated to meet functional needs; 3. Clinical examination findings include all of the following:
clinical_service_or_procedure: Upper Extremity and Myoelectric Prosthetics - Initial Request (HCPCS L6000-L7499)

criteria.description: Functional needs cannot be met with activity modification or compensatory techniques
Requested prosthesis anticipated to meet functional needs
Clinical exam: appropriate residual limb length, stable volume, skin integrity, strength/ROM, cognitive function
Comprehensive rehab plan: pre-prosthetic therapy, control method discussed, task training, home exercise

required_documentation: Prosthetist detailed clinical evaluation and measurements
Physiatry or orthopedic comprehensive limb exam
Comprehensive prosthetic rehabilitation and training plan
review_notes: Requires mandatory secondary review by medical director or therapy advisor.

policy_title: Clinical Policy CP.MP.107: Durable Medical Equipment and Orthotics and Prosthetics Guidelines (Rev. 08/26)
source_quote: Replacement request, all of the following: 1. Replacement is requested due to one of the following: a. Current prosthesis no longer functions properly or physiological or surgical changes to residual limb no longer accommodate current prosthesis; b. Irreparable wear to prosthesis or prosthetic components; c. Significant change in member/enrollee condition resulting in poor fit or function of prosthesis or prosthetic components; 2. Irreparable damage to prosthesis or prosthetic components or repair cost > 60% of replacement cost;
clinical_service_or_procedure: Upper Extremity and Myoelectric Prosthetics - Replacement Request (HCPCS L6000-L7499)

criteria.description: Loss of function, physiological/surgical limb change, irreparable wear, or condition change
Irreparable damage or repair cost exceeds 60% of replacement cost
Prosthesis has been properly cared for following manufacturer recommendations
Medical documentation supports continued use, motivation, appropriate functional level, same/similar components

required_documentation: Detailed repair estimate demonstrating repair cost >60% of replacement
Prosthetist clinical evaluation of limb changes and wear
review_notes: Mandatory 60% repair-cost threshold and secondary review by medical director.

policy_title: Clinical Policy CP.MP.107: Durable Medical Equipment and Orthotics and Prosthetics Guidelines (Rev. 08/26)

clinical_service_or_procedure: Upper Extremity and Myoelectric Prosthetics - Mandatory Secondary Review Requirement

review_notes: Mandatory clinical peer review for all upper extremity and myoelectric prosthetics.

policy_title: Clinical Policy CP.MP.107: Durable Medical Equipment and Orthotics and Prosthetics Guidelines (Rev. 08/26)
source_quote: Requests for facial prosthetics are medically necessary when there is loss or absence of facial tissue due to disease, trauma, surgery, or a congenital defect.
clinical_service_or_procedure: Facial Prosthetics (HCPCS L8040, L8041, L8042, L8043, L8044, L8045, L8046, L8047, L8499)

criteria.description: Loss or absence of facial tissue due to disease, trauma, surgery, or congenital defect

required_documentation: Surgical or clinical notes detailing etiology of facial tissue loss
Anaplastology or prosthetics detailed fabrication plan
review_notes: Covers traumatic, surgical, oncology, or congenital facial tissue absence.

policy_title: Clinical Policy CP.MP.107: Durable Medical Equipment and Orthotics and Prosthetics Guidelines (Rev. 08/26)
source_quote: Medically necessary when used for one of the following indications: A. Iron poisoning when used in the administration of deferoxamine for the treatment of acute iron poisoning and iron overload; B. Chemotherapy for liver cancer when used in the treatment of primary hepatocellular carcinoma or colorectal cancer where the disease is unresectable or where the patient refuses surgical excision of the tumor; C. With opioid drugs when used for intractable pain caused by cancer; D. To administer a drug considered reasonable and necessary by either: 1. Prolonged infusion of at least eight hours because of proven improved clinical efficacy (i.e., proven or generally accepted to have significant advantages over intermittent bolus administration regimens or infusions lasting less than eight hours); 2. Intermittent infusion, each episode of infusion lasting less than eight hours

criteria.description: Deferoxamine for iron poisoning/overload, liver cancer chemo, opioid for cancer pain, or qualifying prolonged/ intermittent infusion

required_documentation: Prescription specifying drug, dosage, and infusion duration
Oncology or clinical notes confirming cancer pain or diagnosis
review_notes: CMS NCD 280.14 aligned criteria for ambulatory infusion.
